column1: # program tests: name, tab, arguments of flucut (see tests/run-case.sh)
# (the built-in references default to FLUCUT_BUILTIN_REFERENCES, set by
# run-case.sh to testdata/ref-ha.fasta, so no download in the tests; the
# the reads with several amplicons written whole, and left out (those
# of the Illumina case, where some reads are split)
# two references, HA and PA (segment 3); the reads are of the HA: with
# --segment HA they are classified as with both references; with
# --segment PA their ends are not located in the HA (two are placed in
# the PA by chance); --report-segment changes only the HTML report
# reads with an internal deletion (the tag ct), each written as its two
# flanks, cut at the junction (the default); the same reads written
# whole, and left out (with a file for each category but theirs); the
# reads written to a file for each category, for each input
# the reads placed on no segment left out
# influenza B: reads of its HA, simulated with the primer pair of the
# HA and the NA (b-hana), against references of its HA and its M
# segment. The last read was primed by the pair of the M segment: its
# end is a segment terminus, but the bases of that primer are not the
# sequence of the HA there, so the whole primer is removed, while the
# other reads keep the terminus (see primers.h)
# the same reads with the primers of both types (the default scheme)
# the primers of influenza A alone
# the scheme chosen from the reads (-s auto): twelve reads have too few
# read ends with a conserved terminus, so the default is used and the
# choice is reported as not found
# two HA references of different subtypes (the second one synthetic);
# reads of the first one alone: no read of a second subtype
# the same with four reads of the second one: reads of a second HA
